subject: VM cadence, SLA acceptance and remediation play
messages:
From: Ella Jones <ella.jones@brightlinepay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@brightlinepay.com
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: VM cadence, SLA acceptance and remediation playbook

Hi Kimberly,

Hope you’re well. BrightLine’s security team is completing our SIG questionnaire and we need a compact package that confirms Redwood’s vulnerability management cadence and SLA commitments for critical/important CVEs, plus a remediation playbook for high‑severity findings. Specifically we need:

- Scan cadence (internal scans + third‑party scans) and time to remediation targets by severity (Critical, High, Medium).
- Evidence of recent scans (last 90 days) and an executive summary we can include in our SIG/CAIQ response.
- An attestation that Redwood will meet our requested SLA for Critical CVEs: 72 hours to patch/mitigate and 7‑day remediation verification OR documented exception process.
- A remediation playbook for triage->hotfix->validation->release, including ownership and rollback steps.

Can you send a single consolidated packet or a short attestation letter and pointers to the artifacts? BrightLine is also asking for any known recent CVEs that required cross‑team coordination (root cause + timeline).

Thanks — we’re on a tight window for the SIG submission (end of week).

Best,
Ella Jones
Security Ops Lead
BrightLine Pay

[Attachment: sig-request-20250414.pdf]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ella Jones <ella.jones@brightlinepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: VM cadence, SLA acceptance and remediation playbook

Hi Ella — thanks for the clear list. We can provide a consolidated packet. High level summary below and I’ll attach the artifacts shortly:

- Scan cadence: weekly internal authenticated scans (dynamic + SCA), third‑party full environment scans every 30 days, and continuous agent telemetry for production instances.
- SLA commitments: Redwood confirms an operational SLA for Critical CVEs as follows: acknowledge within 1 business hour, mitigation plan within 24 hours, and either fix or temporary mitigation deployed within 72 hours for on‑platform services. We will provide a signed SLA letter for BrightLine that documents the exception workflow when third‑party dependencies require vendor timelines.
- Evidence: I’m attaching the latest scan summary (vm_scan_summary_20250401.pdf) and the remediation log for the one recent CVE that required cross‑team coordination (cve-2025-1427‑remediation-log.csv).
- Remediation playbook: triage owner assigned by SRE -> create MAU (mutual action plan) -> canary patch -> verification (automation + manual QA) -> rollout; rollback via hotfix revert and orchestration runbook. Ownership and escalation matrix included in the attached PDF.

Per your ask, I’m also including a signed attestation letter (sla-commitment-letter.pdf). If BrightLine requires the 72hr written commitment specifically in the SIG matrix, the attestation is explicit.

I copied Marissa for legal/contract questions and Lauren for SRE confirmation. Let us know if you need a DocuSign route for the letter.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: vm_scan_summary_20250401.pdf, cve-2025-1427-remediation-log.csv, sla-commitment-letter.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: VM cadence, SLA acceptance and remediation playbook

Kim — quick notes for the packet and JIRA references:

- The CVE referenced (CVE‑2025‑1427) impacted a community dependency; remediation required a vendor PR plus our staging patch. Timeline: discovery 2025‑03‑28, vendor PR 2025‑04‑02, staging validation 04‑04, production rollout 04‑07. We validated remediation and closed the issue on 04‑08.
- I exported the remediation validation steps to cve-2025-1427-remediation-log.csv (attached) — includes timestamps, owners, and test results.
- For BrightLine’s SLA ask: legal prefers the attestation letter but wants a short appendix that calls out third‑party exceptions and the escalation path to request temporary compensating controls. I’ve drafted a 1‑page appendix and saved it to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cd_VM_Evidence.

If Kim signs off, I’ll send the final packet to Ella and route the DocuSign link.

—Marissa
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ella Jones <ella.jones@brightlinepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: VM cadence, SLA acceptance and remediation playbook

Ella — attaching the consolidated packet and the signed attestation. Key highlights in the packet:

- Weekly internal authenticated scans; monthly third‑party full scans; continuous telemetry in prod.
- For Critical CVEs: acknowledge 1 hour, mitigation plan 24 hours, mitigation deployed within 72 hours. We provide documented exception flow when third‑party vendor timelines exceed our window.
- Detailed remediation playbook and ownership matrix; CVE‑2025‑1427 timeline and validation evidence included.

Attachments: vm_scan_summary_20250401.pdf (executive summary), cve-2025-1427-remediation-log.csv (detailed timeline and validation), sla-commitment-letter.pdf (signed attestation).

If BrightLine needs DocuSign, we can send the link here: https://docusign.com/ABC-Redwood-SLA-2025.

We appreciate the heads up on the SIG timeline — happy to hop on a 20‑minute call if your team wants to walk through the packet.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: vm_scan_summary_20250401.pdf, cve-2025-1427-remediation-log.csv, sla-commitment-letter.pdf]
